Package com.codeup.novabook.db

Class ConnectionFactory

java.lang.Object
com.codeup.novabook.db.ConnectionFactory
public class ConnectionFactory extends Object
Database connection factory that implements the Factory Method pattern.

This factory centralizes JDBC connection creation and supports multiple database vendors including PostgreSQL and MySQL. The database configuration is externalized through the AppConfig system, allowing runtime database selection.

Supported Database Vendors:

  • PostgreSQL - When db.vendor=postgres
  • MySQL - When db.vendor=mysql (default)

Usage Example:


 AppConfig config = new AppConfig();
 ConnectionFactory factory = new ConnectionFactory(config);
 
 try (Connection conn = factory.open()) {
     // Use database connection
     PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users");
     // ... perform database operations
 }

Configuration Requirements:

  • db.vendor - Database type (postgres/mysql)
  • db.host - Database server hostname
  • db.port - Database server port
  • db.name - Database name
  • db.user - Database username
  • db.password - Database password
  • db.useSSL - SSL flag (MySQL only)

  • Method Details

    • open

      public Connection open() throws SQLException
      Opens a new database connection based on the configured database vendor.

      This method creates JDBC connections for different database types based on the db.vendor configuration property. It automatically constructs the appropriate JDBC URL and connection parameters.

      PostgreSQL URL Format:
      jdbc:postgresql://host:port/database

      MySQL URL Format:
      jdbc:mysql://host:port/database?useSSL=value&serverTimezone=UTC

      Example:

      
 try (Connection conn = factory.open()) {
     // Connection is automatically closed due to try-with-resources
     PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users");
     ResultSet rs = ps.executeQuery();
     // ... process results
 }
      Returns:
      a new database connection ready for use
      Throws:
      SQLException - if a database access error occurs or connection fails
      IllegalArgumentException - if required configuration properties are missing
